title: When the Ferry Goes Your Way

plate.narration: At Ashspan Bridge, river water taps the ferry landing. A flat boat waits beside its long pole. The road crosses overhead, while the current carries on toward the coast.

goal.text: Get the travelers across the river, then help mend Ashspan Bridge.

steps.label: Get the new planks to the bridge

bridge.narration: A stone bridge called Ashspan Bridge crosses the Great River here, but the melt has taken half the planks from its middle. Old Ossley, a frogfolk boatman, leans on a long pole beside his flat boat. "Changed melt," he says, watching a branch turn in the current. "Busy year. Folk cannot walk over, so they ride with me. Help me get them across, and then the bridge wants mending."

variants.text: He checks the blanket around your shoulders before returning to his pole.

landing.narration: A mooring rope has dragged the landing plank loose, and the plank is wobbling like a loose tooth. Ossley is holding the boat steady with his pole while two travelers wait with their bags. One bag quacks, loudly. The other traveler pretends not to hear it. What will you do?

choices.label: Hold the plank while the travelers board
Help move the rope off the plank
Use brace to hold the plank end like a post

plank_check.prompt: Hold the plank flat and steady while the travelers step aboard. Choose who leads; everyone can help.

rope_check.prompt: Flip the mooring rope off the plank before the boat drifts away. Choose who leads; everyone can help.

brace_check.prompt: A thornguard's brace holds the plank end like a post. Can you walk the heavy bags across it without a wobble?

plank.narration: You hold the plank flat until both travelers are aboard. Ossley tests it once with his pole and nods. "That will do." One traveler pats the plank as she passes, the way you would pat a good horse.

rope.narration: You lift the rope clear and seat the plank on its supports. The travelers board without wetting their bags. Ossley gives you a brief nod, which from a frogfolk boatman is a parade. The loose rope coils itself on the deck like a sleeping snake.

brace_done.narration: The plank end does not move, not even when the heaviest bag thumps across. Both travelers board with dry shoes. Ossley gives the plank an admiring tap. "Like a post," he says. "A post that gets out of the way afterward. Hard to find."

board_wet.narration: The plank tips and one bag drops into the shallows, quacking. Everyone fishes it out together. The travelers board soaked and cheerful. "It floats," says one. "It is a very good bag." Ossley wrings out his hat and says nothing at all, which is how frogfolk laugh.

ferry_ask.narration: The nearer traveler hugs her bag. "Tilly," she says. "Duck eggs, for market across the water. They are not due for days." The bag quacks. "They disagree." Ossley pushes off, and the bridge slides slowly past overhead, full of holes like cheese. "The river is strong this year, and a flat boat spins when the weight sits wrong," he says. The current tugs at the boat like a dog at a sleeve.

ferry_plan.narration: Ossley hands out jobs. "The boat needs steadying, and the river needs watching," he says. "I only have the two eyes, and one of them is on my hat." The far landing looks very small from here. How will you help get across?

choices.label: Take the pole with Ossley and push against the current
Fly ahead and watch for snags in the water

pole_check.prompt: Take the pole beside Ossley and push against the current, stroke after stroke. Choose who leads; everyone can help.

watch_check.prompt: Wings lift you above the water to watch for snags. Can you call a safe line back to Ossley?

ferry_hold.prompt: Ossley calls the lean! Everyone shift your weight the same way, then back, and keep the flat boat from spinning!

crossing.narration: You lean left, then right, then left again. The flat boat wobbles like a duck and slides across, straight as a plank. "Good," says Ossley. "Frogfolk dislike spinning." He bumps the far landing as gently as a sleepy cat. Tilly counts her eggs, which takes no time, since they are all in one bag. The bag quacks the total.

ferry_spin.narration: The boat does one slow circle. The bridge goes by twice. Ossley says nothing, but his throat puffs out like a drum. Then he drives the pole into the mud and the boat stops, a little dizzy, a little late. Tilly checks her eggs. "Still quacking," she says, and everyone breathes again.

ferry_dock.narration: The far landing is coming up fast. Ossley sets his pole like a brake. "Easy," he says. "Bump, do not crash. Tell me when." Tilly covers her bag with both hands.

interaction.cue: Tap when the boat swings level with the landing.

onSuccess.narration: A gentle bump. The flat boat stops like a sleepy cat, and the eggs do not even quack.

onFailure.narration: The boat kisses the dock a little hard. The eggs quack, and Ossley's throat puffs. "Landed," he says. "Technically."

onAssisted.narration: Ossley eases the pole and the boat slides in all by itself, and he pretends it was you.

far_bank.narration: The far landing has a muddy ramp and a heap of old planks piled at its edge. A dragonling bridge-mender named Bryn stands with her hands on her hips, glaring at the broken deck. "Planks, I have," she says, "up the bank in my cart. Hands, I do not. Help me fix this, and the market folk can cross, and Ossley can rest his pole." Tilly nods hard. "And my eggs can get to market," she says. Ossley says nothing, but his pole sags with relief.

plank_pile.narration: Bryn nods at the heap of old planks lying on the ramp. "That pile has to move before my cart can come down," she says. "It has been there since dawn. I think it has also been breathing." The pile gives a small, damp sigh. Tilly holds her bag tighter.

choices.label: Poke the pile with Ossley's pole
Stamp on the ramp to see what jumps

poke_reveal.narration: You poke the pile with Ossley's pole. The pile blinks. Eyes open under the top plank, then a wide wet mouth, then stubby legs. It is a pair of mire mimics, a big one and a little one, marsh creatures that dress up as whatever lies on the ground and wait for a snack. They have been hungry since dawn, and Tilly's bag smells very like duck.

stamp_reveal.narration: You stamp the ramp, thump, thump, thump, and the whole pile jumps. Under the top plank a mouth opens, and stubby legs unfold. It is a pair of mire mimics, a big one and a little one, marsh creatures that dress up as whatever lies on the ground and wait for a snack. They have been hungry since dawn, and Tilly's bag smells very like duck.

mimic_fight.narration: The two mire mimics wobble up on their little legs, planks clattering down their backs. They do not want to hurt anybody. They want a snack, a nap and to be left alone, in that order. Shoo them back to the reeds before they eat Tilly's bag!

mimic_won.narration: The mimics give a surprised hiccup, drop their planks, and waddle off toward the reeds to find nicer ground to pretend to be. They leave behind a bootlace one of them once swallowed. "Not mine," says Bryn. "Yours." Ossley nods. "Good. It is hard to unload a pile that argues."

mimic_shooed.narration: The mimics are faster than they look, and you end up sitting in the mud with a plank on your head. Ossley hooks the big mimic's top plank with his pole and tips it, whump, back into the reeds, and the little one follows. "They like a good fuss," he says. He pours you warm tea from a flask. Bryn rubs the mud from your ear. Up the bank, a cart waits in the mud.

cart_plan.narration: The cart that carries the new planks sits in mud up to its axle. Bryn's two pack goats strain at the front, but they only slip. One of them sits down, as if to say, call me when it's over. How will you get the cart out?

choices.label: Lay old planks under the wheel as a track
Use roar to start the goats pulling together

dig_check.prompt: Dig the mud from around the wheel and push the cart out. Choose who leads; everyone can help.

track_check.prompt: Work out where the old planks must lie so the wheel can climb out of the mud. Choose who leads; everyone can help.

roar_check.prompt: A manticore's roar startles the goats into pulling together. Can you steer the cart straight out of the mud?

cart_free.narration: The wheel pops out of the mud with a slurp. The goats trot up the bank as if it had been their idea all along, and the cart rolls toward the bridge with a creak. Bryn counts the planks twice. "All there," she says, and kisses the nearest goat on the nose. The goat looks away, deeply embarrassed, and eats her sleeve.

choices.label: Carry the planks to the bridge

cart_stuck.narration: You push, the cart sinks, and the mud wins. In the end Ossley's mooring rope and everyone's backs haul it out together, but one plank snaps on the way. Bryn holds up the two halves. "Kindling," she says. "I will make do." She hands you a brave whistle from her belt. "For calling goats. They ignore it, but it is very loud." The goats stand a long way off, pretending to be somebody else's goats.

choices.label: Carry the planks to the bridge

unload_relay.narration: The cart cannot cross the broken bridge end, so the planks must go by hand. Bryn stands at the bridge. The rest of you make a line, and one goat watches the whole thing, unhelpfully.

interaction.cue: Catch a plank, then pass it down the line.

onSuccess.narration: Plank after plank goes hand to hand, tap, tap, tap, until the stack stands at the bridge end.

onFailure.narration: A plank slips from the line and lands in the mud with a flat splat. Bryn scrapes it clean, but it is cracked.

onAssisted.narration: Bryn takes the middle of the line herself, and the planks fly down it like loaves at a bakery.

bridge_head.narration: The planks are stacked at the bridge end. At the first stone pier, logs and branches have jammed into a heap. The river is pushing the whole heap against the stone. "Debris," says Bryn. "The river has thrown its furniture at us." If the heap shifts, it will shove the bridge crooked. Ossley sniffs. "I have seen it do worse. Not often. But I have."

jam_plan.narration: The jam is a heap of logs, roots and one entire fence. Ossley squints at it. "Pull the wrong log and the rest may roll." What will you do about the jam?

choices.label: Hook the logs out one at a time
Tie a rope round the heap and everyone pulls
Have a duskrunner slip along the pier and free the key log

hook_check.prompt: Hook each log with the long pole and draw it clear of the pier. Choose who leads; everyone can help.

haul_check.prompt: Everyone take the rope. Pull the whole heap loose together, on Ossley's call!

slip_check.prompt: A duskrunner slips along the pier and spots the key log. Can you pull it out cleanly?

jam_shift.narration: The heap lurches and the pier shudders. A plank slides off the cart and splashes in. Ossley hooks it back with his pole before the river can take it, and the pier is still straight. "Rude," he tells the river, quite loudly. The river, being a river, does not apologize.

jam_clear.narration: The last log slides free and bobs away. One log floats upriver for a few lengths, as if it changed its mind, then turns around and follows the rest. Ossley watches it go. "Changed melt," he says again, more quietly this time. The pier stands straight, and the deck waits above it with a cracked middle beam. Even the goats look thoughtful.

carry_beam.narration: Bryn climbs down to the pier and points under the deck. The middle beam is cracked right through. A new beam lies on the bank, thick as a sleeping cow, and it has to travel to the pier. Everyone takes a place along it. Bryn walks backward in front, calling, "Level! Level! Mostly level!"

interaction.cue: Lift or lower your end until the beam rides level in the middle.

onSuccess.narration: The beam rides level all the way to the pier, like a very long and serious tray.

onFailure.narration: The beam tips and bonks a goat on the rump. The goat is more surprised than hurt. You set it down and carry it again, slower.

onAssisted.narration: Bryn takes the middle of the beam, and it rides level the whole way.

beam_plan.narration: The new beam must go up and into its notches, level, with nobody underneath. How will you raise it?

choices.label: Everyone lifts it together on Ossley's count
Roll it up on log rollers
Have a bigfoot smash the old beam out of its notches
Have a songkeeper hum a count everyone can lift to

lift_check.prompt: Everyone take hold of the beam. Lift together when Ossley counts three!

roll_check.prompt: Set the rollers and the slope so the beam rolls up instead of sticking. Choose who leads; everyone can help.

smash_check.prompt: A bigfoot's smash knocks the cracked beam loose. Can you slide the new one into the empty notches?

hum_check.prompt: A songkeeper's hum keeps the count. Can you keep the beam level while everyone lifts?

beam_up.narration: The beam slides into its notches with a deep thunk. Bryn pats it like a pony. "Good beam," she says. "Do not tell the old one it was replaced." Ossley taps it with his pole. It rings, deep and clear. Somewhere in the stone, the whole bridge seems to relax, like a cat settling on a warm step.

beam_slip.narration: The beam sags and thumps into the notches off by a finger, scraping everyone's hands. Bryn taps it with a mallet until it sits straight. "It was shy," she says. "Now it is brave." Ossley taps it with his pole. It rings, a bit flat, but it rings. Bryn passes around her lunch pail: a supper bundle, still warm.

hatch.narration: Tilly's bag cracks. A tiny beak pokes out. "Oh no," says Tilly. "Oh yes," says Ossley. A duckling the size of a teacup tumbles out, then another, then a whole fluffy handful. They waddle straight toward the gap in the deck, singing one word, which is "peep."

duck_play.narration: Tilly's bag is mostly feathers now. The ducklings peep in a circle round everyone's boots, too excited to listen to anybody.

interaction.cue: Everyone, settle the ducklings with something gentle.

options.label: Scatter oat crumbs
options.reaction: The ducklings tumble after the crumbs in a fluffy rush.

options.label: Pet a soft little head
options.reaction: A duckling leans into your hand and closes its eyes.

options.label: Hum a slow tune
options.reaction: The peeping slows down to match your humming.

onSuccess.narration: The ducklings settle into one warm heap, every one of them yawning.

onFailure.narration: A few ducklings keep peeping, but they stay close to your boots.

onAssisted.narration: Tilly tucks the ducklings into her hat, and they quiet down at once.

duck_plan.narration: The ducklings are calmer now, but very curious. The nearest wanders to the edge of the bridge head and looks down at the water with great interest. "Eggs," says Tilly faintly, "are supposed to wait until market." How will you get them to safety?

choices.label: Scoop them up in Tilly's basket
Coax them with a low, calm voice
Use beguile to draw a bright trail they will follow

scoop_check.prompt: Sweep the ducklings into the basket before they reach the gap. Choose who leads; everyone can help.

coax_check.prompt: Crouch low and call to the ducklings softly until they follow you. Choose who speaks; everyone can help.

trail_check.prompt: A kitsune's beguile draws a bright trail through the air. Can you lead the ducklings along it and into the basket?

ducks_safe.narration: The ducklings tumble into the basket in a fluffy heap and go quiet at once. Tilly counts, loses count, and counts again. "All of them," she says. "My heroes." One duckling climbs onto Ossley's hat and falls asleep. He does not move for a long time, for fear of the peeping. Tilly ties a songbird ribbon round your wrist. "For the heroes," she says.

ducks_loose.narration: Three ducklings dart through to the edge of the gap and cling to a plank end, peeping furiously. Ossley fishes them out with his pole and net, dripping and unimpressed. One pecks your ankle. Tilly gathers all of them into her hat. "They'll learn," she says. "Eventually. Possibly in about a year." She ties a songbird ribbon round your wrist. "For the heroes," she says.

planks_plan.narration: Now the deck. Bryn's planks wait on the bank, and the gap yawns between the two ends of the bridge. How will you get the planks across?

choices.label: Slide the planks across on a rope line
Pass them hand to hand along the bridge
Carry the plank line across on wings

rope2_check.prompt: Slide each plank along the rope line, tap it into place, and send the next. Choose who leads; everyone can help.

pass_check.prompt: Pass each plank hand to hand with a steady rhythm. Choose who sets the beat; everyone can help.

pwing_check.prompt: Wings carry the line across the gap. Can you land every plank square?

planks_dropped.narration: A plank slips off the line and slaps into the river. Ossley hooks it with his pole and drags it dripping to the landing, grumbling about wet wood. It takes two trips and a very damp plank, but the deck gets laid. Bryn wrings out the plank like laundry.

planks_laid.narration: The planks go down one by one, tap tap tap, until the deck has only one small hole left, about the size of a goat. Bryn fits the last plank with a mallet. "Now," she says, "it needs tying down, so it stays put when the river sulks." One of the goats looks at the last hole, then at Bryn, then very slowly walks away.

variants.text: One plank went to the mud, so Ossley gives up a spare board from his boat. He does not say a word, but he is sniffing.

lash_plan.narration: Bryn taps a loose plank. "A deck stays only if it is tied down." The long ropes wait in a coil, the pegs in a bucket. How will you lash the planks?

choices.label: Tie every plank to the beams with careful knots
Have a duskrunner secure the loose straps
Blow the brave whistle to bring the goats to pull

knots_check.narration: You tie the plank ends to the beams while Bryn checks each knot.

pegs_check.narration: You drive the pegs while Bryn holds the planks square.

whistle_check.narration: The whistle brings the goats. Ossley hitches them to the line, and you walk it tight together.

straps_check.narration: Your duskrunner secures the straps while friends hold the loose ends.

lashed.narration: The last knot snaps tight, and the deck stops creaking. Bryn walks its whole length like a cat that owns the place. "One more thing," she says. "A bridge has to carry everyone at once. Not one at a time, like a polite bridge. Everyone, on the deck, now. Ossley too." Ossley sighs and hops up.

test_check.narration: You walk the finished deck with Bryn, stopping at each plank. "Fastenings first," she says. "Then I call the travelers."

bridge_open.narration: Every plank holds. Bryn does a small dance, then pretends she did not. At the far end, the market folk, who have been waiting all afternoon with baskets on their heads, start across in a long, chattering line. For one beautiful moment, everything is exactly as it should be.

folk_cross.narration: The market folk file across the mended deck. Tilly follows, with her basket of peeping ducklings. She stops by Ossley. "I would have missed market," she says. "Thank you." Ossley takes off his hat. "The river brought you my way," he says. "I only had to be going it." He puts the hat back on, then, very carefully, checks it for ducks. Bryn pays you six coins from the toll box, since a bridge should pay its menders.

choices.label: See what Tilly wants to give

gift_plan.narration: Tilly rummages in her bag, which is now mostly feathers. "I have to give you something," she says. "I have oat cakes, and I have a story about a goose. The oat cakes are better. The story is longer." Bryn leans on her mallet and waits, too.

choices.label: Ask for the story about the goose
Buy a bag of Tilly's oat cakes (3 coins)

buy_cakes.narration: Tilly counts out a bag of oat cakes and takes your three coins with great seriousness, then gives one coin back for luck. Then she takes it back. "No," she says. "Business is business." The cakes are still warm and have a faint smell of duckling.

cakes.narration: Tilly presses a warm bundle of oat cakes into your hands. They smell of butter and the inside of a good oven. "Do not share them with ducks," she says. "They will take advantage." A duckling peeps from the basket, exactly as if it were being accused.

goose.narration: Tilly tells the story of the goose who tried to marry a weathervane. It takes a long time and has three endings. Ossley falls asleep halfway through, standing up, and Bryn pretends not to notice. You find that you like the goose very much, and the weathervane a little less.

rest_hut.narration: Bryn lights a small stove in the bridge-house. It smells of hot oats and slightly of goat. The sun slides low over the river, and the new deck glows like a table after supper. Ossley points to a raised footpath into the Whispering Marsh. "There is a school called the Academy in the village up there," he says. "They made me a dry reed mat for my deck, and nobody has fetched it. Follow the posts. The ducks take shortcuts. You should not."

choices.label: Sit on the new deck and dangle your feet
Help Ossley tie up his boat for the night
Share your supper with Bryn and Ossley
Visit the Academy in the marsh

share_bryn.narration: You set out your supper, and Bryn adds her oats, and Ossley adds a fish that nobody asked about. It is a very odd meal and a very good one. Afterward Bryn hangs a river charm round your neck. "A bridge-mender's thanks," she says. "It keeps the wet out of your boots. Mostly."

dangle.narration: The deck is warm from the sun. Below your feet the river goes by, busy and brown. Ossley sits beside you and tells you the names of seven fish he has argued with. The worst, he says, is called Gerald. Gerald, apparently, always wins. He says it with great respect, and a little with his hat.

tie_boat.narration: Ossley shows you his favorite knot, the one that comes undone when he whistles. You practice until it only comes undone when you whistle. He looks at it for a long time. "You are a natural," he says, "or a menace." He has not decided which.

ossley_routes.narration: Ossley coils his rope. "Tomorrow's tide takes me downriver," he says. "The coast down there is called the Saltrot, and it is not like here." He points the other way, up the road. "Or there are the old boundary stones, where the keepers count things. Ask me one, and I will tell you what I know."

choices.label: Ask about the stone keepers up the road

coast_talk.narration: "Salt flats and silt," says Ossley. "This year the silt came from nowhere I know. A flood year, the kind where a boat can go places it should not." He pats his pole. "I will be going that way again, and I will take whoever wants to come. I am generally going your way." Then he looks at his hat. "Sometimes the river even agrees."

inland_talk.narration: "The keepers up the road count old stones," says Ossley. "They have been asking the river questions for years, and the river never answers in the same order. Ask them nicely. Bring a cheese, if you have one." He blinks both eyelids at once, which means a joke.

routes.narration: Ossley points downriver, toward the coast called the Saltrot, and then up the road toward the boundary stones. The bridge behind you is whole, and the landing is safe. He marks an upper bank road north to a landing called Frostfang Shore. "Dry ground. Long walk. Griffin country at the far end." Whichever way you go, you have a boatman who is generally going the same way. The river goes on, busy as ever, carrying its furniture.

marsh_path.narration: The raised path carries you into the Whispering Marsh. Reeds brush your sleeves. Ahead, a village stands on wooden legs above the water. A rolled reed mat waits beside a notice: "For the ferry. Please keep dry." A puddle fills the last stretch of path. How will you carry the mat back?

choices.label: Carry it high above the puddle
Wrap it in your dry cloak

mat_high.narration: You lift the mat overhead and carry it to a dry bench in the village. A duck walks under it. For a moment, the duck has a roof.

mat_wrap.narration: You wrap the mat in a dry cloak and carry it to a bench in the village. Water splashes your ankles. The mat stays dry. Your socks are less lucky.

village_rest.narration: You rest beside the dry mat in the marsh village. A round tower rises above the reeds. It has no roof. A page of homework floats down and lands on a duck. The duck looks pleased with its marks. The posted path will take you back to the ferry.

choices.label: Climb the tower with no roof
Carry the mat back to the ferry

mat_return.narration: You follow the posts out of the marsh and back to the bridge. Ossley unrolls the dry mat across his wet deck. The travelers step onto it without slipping. "Better," he says. He tucks a corner under a rope so it will stay put.

academy.narration: Above the marsh village, at the top of the tower is a classroom with no roof at all, only sky. This school is called the Academy. Here students learn to be a Starweaver, a hero who reads the stars. A dragonling named Professor Nettle stands beside a huge brass telescope. Homework floats up off the desks and drifts away over the reeds. Nobody chases it. "It comes down somewhere," says the professor. On a cushion sits a star circlet. A Starweaver's light lives in that circlet, and a dusk hood worn beside it starts to itch. "Anyone who wants the circlet," says Professor Nettle, "may try it on."

variants.text: Professor Nettle waves from beside the big brass telescope. "Back at the Academy! Mind the homework." A page floats past your nose and off over the reeds. The star circlet waits on its cushion for anyone who wants to try it on.

academy_stars.narration: Professor Nettle lets you look through the telescope. Even by day, the stars are so close you could count their points. Then the telescope sneezes. Brass rattles. Dust puffs out of the far end. "Bless you," says the professor, to the telescope. "It does that when it sees something new."

voiceGuide.tone: Warm, funny, curious, with real consequences. Describe actions and sensory details directly. Short dialogue. Never use "the kind of thing that", "the sort of thing that", or "it was X, the type of thing that makes you Y" comparisons. Let a character act instead of explaining how the reader should feel.
voiceGuide.vocabulary: Read aloud to an eight-year-old. Concrete words, short sentences, distinct voices.
